result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You had a thyroid blood test (TFT) on 25 September 2026. It is a blood test of the thyroid gland.
Your TSH was 7.8 mU/L. The normal range is 0.3 to 4.2.
This means your dose of levothyroxine is too low.
So your dose is going up. You also need another blood test.

## What you need to do
1. Collect your new prescription from your pharmacy. It is ready now.
2. Take one 25 micrograms tablet and one 50 micrograms tablet every day.
3. Take levothyroxine on an empty stomach. Wait at least 30 minutes before breakfast or other medicines.
4. Leave at least 4 hours between levothyroxine and iron or calcium tablets.
5. Do not take levothyroxine at the same time as iron or calcium tablets.
6. Have a repeat TFT blood test in 6 to 8 weeks.

## Dates and medicines
- 25 September 2026: you had your thyroid blood test (TFT).
- 6 November 2026 to 20 November 2026: have your repeat TFT blood test.

Medicine: levothyroxine
- Dose now: 75 micrograms, once a day.
- What changed: it went up from 50 micrograms.
- The 75 micrograms is one 25 micrograms tablet plus one 50 micrograms tablet. Take them together every day.
- Take it on an empty stomach, at least 30 minutes before breakfast or other medicines.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- What is levothyroxine, and what does it do?
- Who will book my repeat blood test?
- How do I fit my iron or calcium tablets around levothyroxine?

## When to get urgent help
The letter does not list specific warning signs.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
